report:
### Conclusion
The health claim is **true** based on clinical evidence. High-quality randomized controlled trials and systematic reviews demonstrate that chlorhexidine-alcohol skin preparation before cesarean delivery significantly reduces the risk of surgical-site infection (SSI) compared with iodine-alcohol or povidone-iodine.

### Evidence Summary
* **Landmark Trial:** A randomized trial published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* showed that preoperative skin preparation with chlorhexidine–alcohol resulted in a significantly lower risk of SSI after cesarean delivery than iodine–alcohol (relative risk 0.55; 95% CI, 0.34–0.90) (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1511048).
* **Cochrane Systematic Review:** A Cochrane review concluded with moderate-certainty evidence that preparing the skin with chlorhexidine gluconate before a cesarean section is more effective at reducing SSIs than povidone-iodine (https://www.cochrane.org/CD007462/PREG_skin-preparation-preventing-infection-following-caesarean-section).
* **Broad Meta-Analyses:** Updated network meta-analyses and practice recommendations note that chlorhexidine-alcohol significantly lowers SSI rates compared to povidone-iodine (risk ratio 0.72; 95% CI, 0.58–0.91 across 8 randomized trials) (https://obgyn.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ijgo.15117).

While a few individual studies (such as the CAPICA trial) found comparable outcomes between regimens, the consensus across large trials and systematic reviews favors chlorhexidine-alcohol.
